subject: Civil Engineering
title: Traffic Calming: Slowing Cars Down
description: A short lesson to help you apply Traffic Calming: Slowing Cars Down.

hook.text: Neighborhood streets designed like highways invite speeding. The design must change.

buildup.text: Speed bumps force drivers to slow down. Chicanes make drivers weave through offsets.

discovery.text: Narrowing lanes with curb extensions makes drivers feel the road is tighter — they slow.

twist.text: Raised crosswalks prioritize pedestrians and force cars to yield physically.

climax.text: Woonerf streets in the Netherlands share space equally — cars crawl at walking pace.

punchline.text: Design the street for slow speeds and drivers obey without signs.

quiz.question: How does narrowing a lane calm traffic?
options: It blocks larger vehicles from entering the street
Drivers perceive a tighter road and instinctively reduce speed
It increases traffic congestion, forcing everyone to stop
